checks.name: concurrent last slot (observed lock wait): the signup callback holds the code row before commit; the waiting POST /invite/validate is the neutral refusal, performs no PAR and no second create; exactly one pending admission is then admitted, and a later validate stays refused

identical retries (observed lock wait): two verified sign-ins of one pending identity return one stored admission, one principal, one entitlement and one admission.redeemed; each completion mints its own session

expired entitlement is not revived: a sign-in stopped after the member fence, before the entitlement re-read, is denied once the expiry is committed; the existing sessions are the uniform 404, a later sign-in stays denied, and no entitlement row is added

entitlement revocation racing a sign-in (observed lock wait): the operator waits on the member fence until the mint commits, then the new session and the earlier session are the uniform 404 and a later sign-in is denied without a new entitlement

admission-first: code revocation waits on the code row until the sign-in commits; the admission stands, the code is then revoked, and a later sign-in replays the stored admission without a second slot

revocation-first (observed lock wait): the verified sign-in waits behind the code-row update and is denied with no principal, membership or entitlement; the pending admission is denied_for_reconciliation and a later sign-in stays denied

create dropped before a response is unknown, not sent again; reconcile inside the grace leaves it unknown and, after the row is aged, records failed by inspection with no second POST; public validate is the neutral refusal and mints nothing

create timeout: one POST, an unknown outcome inside the client deadline, no capability; reconcile does not judge it inside the grace and afterwards confirms the invitation by inspection and revokes it (the token was lost) without a second create; public validate mints nothing

revoke timeout: the local code stays revoked and the capability is gone when the remote answer is unknown; the verified sign-in mints nothing; reconcile retries the revocation to confirmed without a second create, and the sign-in stays denied

signup after local expiry is denied and recorded for reconciliation, with no principal or entitlement; an outstanding signup callback after a competing fixture admission takes the last slot is denied, with no live session, principal, membership, entitlement, or second redeemed slot. record_pending_admission returns exhausted without a denied_for_reconciliation row; that audit belongs to admit_redemption when a pending admission already exists
remote revocation propagation: reconcile records the provider's revoked invitation, removes the capability and does not create another; the code stays active and public validate mints nothing

restart/reopen: a replaced Auth and router in this same process, on the same stores, admits no earlier session, completes no earlier pre-login flow and rejects the earlier synchronizer token; the pending identity can resend from a fresh page; a current member signs in again; a revoked member stays denied; an unspent code still validates from the capability directory. This is auth-memory and CSRF replacement, not an operating-system process or storage-pool restart

limits: The provider is the cfg(test) synthetic loopback issuer plus app/runtime/fake_fauth.py. No deployed fAuth, mail, browser or AWS call.
Races stop on the cfg(test) admission checkpoints or on a PostgreSQL lock wait (pg_stat_activity). The provider deadline is the create/revoke timeout itself.

One server-only invitation is single-use and email-bound, so two subjects do not both complete hosted registration on one code. The outstanding callback is prepared while the code is valid; a fixture admission then takes the last slot; the original callback is completed after that. The replaced Auth in the restart check is the same process and the same stores.
Raw codes and invitation tokens are not written to this report.
scope: APP-082 route-level invitation races and provider faults on the local PostgreSQL TLS fixture with the synthetic issuer and loopback fAuth stand-in
